StackType.issue: PowerStackType.Single, and this is the one unit in the on_stack family that goes the OTHER way: the sim does NOT override on_stack, so a second application adds. That happens to be what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236), so it is *more* faithful than the 15 units that override it to `pass` -- but it is still a gap, because C#'s AfterApplied fires only on a genuinely new power while the sim's __init__-time Minion grant (powers.py:1562-1564) likewise only runs on construction. Dormant: nothing reads Illusion's Amount, and the sim's stacking path (cmds.py:308-322) would not re-run __init__ anyway. Recorded so the inconsistency between this unit and its 15 siblings is visible.

ShouldPowerBeRemovedOnDeath.issue: IllusionPower.cs:59-66 keeps the owner's BUFFS (including itself) through death and drops only non-ITemporaryPower Debuffs -- the source comment explains that Temporary powers are excluded so the temp powers THEY applied also go away. The sim has no `should_power_be_removed_on_death` hook (hooks.py defines none) and never removes powers on death at all, so the whole predicate is unreachable in the sim. Dormant on the buff half (the sim keeps everything, which is what this override asks for) and a gap on the DEBUFF half: the game clears the Illusion's Vulnerable/Weak/Frail on its death and the sim carries them into the revived creature, so a revived Illusion is weaker in the sim than in the game. Reachability is the honest limit here -- the sim's only Illusion applier would need naming, and `grep IllusionPower` outside powers.py finds no sim applier at all, so this is dormant with the trigger being **porting any IllusionPower applier** (Parafright is named at IllusionPower.cs:130 and is unported). ITemporaryPower has no sim analogue either (there is no `dark_shackles`-style wrapper in the ported set that survives here). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterApplied.rationale: C# grants MinionPower 1 from AfterApplied unless the owner already has it (IllusionPower.cs:68-75, applier null, cardSource null); the sim does it in __init__ with the same `"minion" not in owner.powers` test (powers.py:1562-1564) and the same absent applier. The sim has no AfterApplied slot, and __init__ runs at exactly the point PowerCmd.apply creates the power (cmds.py:324-327) -- i.e. BEFORE hooks.on_power_applied rather than after, which is the only difference and is unobservable because no ported listener reacts to a Minion grant. Named per the main report's section 7 item 6: the mechanism is __init__-for-AfterApplied, and it would break for any AfterApplied body that needs the power to already be registered.

AfterDeath.issue: Same wrong-hook shape as AdaptablePower's, and not re-argued here: C# lets the death happen and retains the corpse; the sim prevents the death and floors the owner at 1 HP (cmds.py:112). Consequences (1) HP 1 vs 0 and (2) damage_pipeline gap G4's killing-blow-skip recomputation apply identically. The (3) Feed consequence does NOT apply here and it is worth saying why: IllusionPower auto-applies MinionPower, whose ShouldOwnerDeathTriggerFatal() is false, so C# also refuses the fatal -- which is exactly what cards/feed.py:17-18's docstring claims, correctly for Illusion and incorrectly for Adaptable. Additionally absent: C#'s AfterDeath installs a synthetic REVIVE_MOVE MoveState whose FollowUpStateId is `FollowUpStateId ?? MoveStateMachine.StateLog.Last().Id` and whose MustPerformOnceBeforeTransitioning is true (IllusionPower.cs:83-88) -- the sim has no such splice, leaving the revive to the owner's own take_turn calling `revive()` (powers.py:1577-1581), so the move the owner resumes on after reviving is whatever its machine says rather than the logged one. Dormant on that last point only because no sim applier exists. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

ShouldAllowHitting.issue: LIVE, and it upgrades a seam gap that was recorded as un-demonstrated. C#'s PowerCmd.Apply<T> refuses to apply anything to a creature `CanReceivePowers` says no to, and CanReceivePowers reuses Hook.ShouldAllowHitting -- which is exactly what this override's own doc comment says it is for ("This is so the ... doesn't receive POWERS while it is reviving"). The sim wires should_allow_hitting into DamageCmd.deal (cmds.py:51-52) but NOT into PowerCmd.apply, which has no such guard at all. That is `power_cmd` gap **G6**, whose text says "No concrete broken interaction is demonstrated (spot-checked callers apply powers only to already-resolved targets)". **That is now falsified. EXECUTED:** a TEST_SUBJECT_BOSS combat (the Test Subject starts with powers ['adaptable', 'enrage']), a lethal Strike, then Vulnerable 2 from the player -- the sim reports `is_reviving True`, `should_allow_hitting(ts) False`, and then still lands `Vulnerable(2)` on the reviving boss, where the game refuses the application outright. Control: a 10-damage Strike in the same window returns 0 HP lost, proving the predicate IS wired into the damage path and only the power path is missing it. Rule-6 co-occurrence: the Test Subject is the ported Act-3 Glory boss and applies this power to itself at combat start, Bash/Vulnerable is ported basic-pool Ironclad content, and the revive window is the remainder of the player's turn after the killing blow -- the ordinary flow of the fight, not a contrived state. The same override exists on IllusionPower and ReattachPower, so all three carry it. Verdict carried per rule 3; the seam record is not edited (half B does not own audits/seam/** or docs/audit/seams/**) -- reported in .superpowers/sdd/content-power-report-b.md section 2.3. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

guards.issue: A public settable property with no sim analogue: it lets an applier choose which state the revived creature resumes on, defaulting to the last LOGGED state. Folded into the AfterDeath entry; carried separately because it survives a should_die-to-AfterDeath fix. Dormant with the same trigger (no ported applier).
